record.title: fix: let a wrong approval rule be corrected, and hold the edit to the checks the creation passed

notes: Verified the tests actually bind: reverting updateWorkflow to `steps = raw(in.Steps)` makes both new Go tests fail (workflowsteps_test.go:61 sweep + :166/:174 API walk); the frontend tests exercise a 수정 button and PATCH call that do not exist on main. Not vacuous.

Ran everything: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./cmd/... ./internal/...`, full `go test ./...` against a throwaway postgres (VENDRA_TEST_DSN) — all pass, including the new integration test; web `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint .` and all 12 vitest files / 51 tests pass. Worktree left clean, test container removed.

validWorkflowSteps edge cases check out: a JSON null element is refused by the name check before `step["order"]=i` would touch a nil map (no panic); a non-list value fails Unmarshal into []map[string]any and 400s; `in.Steps == nil` on PATCH still keeps the stored steps, and workflowsteps_test.go:244-251 asserts that an enabled-only edit does not rewrite them.

Editing steps cannot disturb approvals already in flight: submitObject snapshots steps into workflow_instances.context and instanceSteps (workflows.go:21) prefers the snapshot over the definition. The comment on WorkflowForm claims exactly this and matches the code.

Risk-condition round-trip is safe: the form's LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL options match riskGradeField, and conditions the form never shows (e.g. riskLevels, securityLevel) are carried through by the `...(workflow?.conditions ?? {})` spread — covered by admin-workflow.test.tsx. `conditions` typed as Record<string,unknown> is still null-safe via optional chaining and `?? {}`.

No new authorization surface: PATCH /api/v1/workflows/{id} already existed behind require("workflow.update") (app.go:235); this only gives it a caller. No migration and no external state change — plain revert restores prior behaviour (a rule created disabled would come back as an uneditable disabled rule, which is the pre-change status quo).

Minor, pre-existing: WorkflowForm.submit awaits post/patch with no try/catch, so a 400 (e.g. a step name left blank) leaves the modal open with no message and an unhandled rejection. Same pattern as the create-only form on main and as other Admin.tsx forms, so not introduced here — worth a follow-up.

Minor: TestAnApprovalRuleCanBeCorrectedWhereItWasWritten deletes every `object_type='payment'` workflow definition on entry and in cleanup, which is broader than what it created. Harmless today because package tests run sequentially and nothing seeds a payment rule, but it is a shared-fixture side effect if these tests are ever run in parallel.

Scope is clean: the workflowtype_test.go change is only the NewWorkflow→WorkflowForm rename the panel refactor forces, and that test still guards the 업무 유형 option list (no role option value collides with an object type name).
